Clarke County, Virginia Tax Sales: Simple Guide to Buying Property at Auction

Clarke County, Virginia holds tax sales when property owners don’t pay their taxes. These auctions help the county recover unpaid taxes while giving buyers a chance to purchase properties at a discount. If you want to get involved, here’s a straightforward guide to how tax sales work in Clarke County.

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

When Clarke County Schedules Tax Sales

There’s no fixed calendar for tax sales in Clarke County. Auctions are held only when enough properties are ready to be sold.

  • How Often: Scheduled as needed
  • Where to Find Dates: Check the Auction Calendar or visit the Treasurer’s Office website

Auction Time and Location

The county runs both online and in-person auctions, depending on the sale.

  • Time: Online auctions usually close around 11:00 AM (ET)
  • Location Options:
    • Online sales happen at ForSaleAtAuction.biz
    • In-person sale addresses are listed in the public auction notice

Registration Details

You must register before bidding, whether the auction is online or in person.

  • Is Registration Required? Yes
  • When to Register:
    • Registration opens with the auction announcement
    • It closes shortly before the sale ends
  • How to Register: Follow the instructions in the auction listing

Can Property Owners Redeem Before the Auction?

Yes, but only up to the day of the auction.

  • Before Auction Day: Owners can pay all overdue taxes to keep the property
  • After the Sale: They lose the right to redeem it

Bidding and Payment Process

If you win a property, you’ll need to pay quickly and follow the sale terms.

  • Winning the Bid: Highest bid wins
  • Buyer’s Premium:
    • 10% added to the final bid (minimum $150)
  • Payment Deadline:
    • Full payment is usually due by the next business day after the auction
  • Accepted Payments: Listed in the auction terms

Where to Get Updates and Listings

For current auctions and updates, check these sites:

  • Clarke County Treasurer’s Office Website
  • Online Auction Platform: ForSaleAtAuction.biz

Contact Info for Help

If you have questions, get in touch with:

  • Clarke County Treasurer’s Office
  • Email: treasurer@clarkecounty.gov
  • Phone: (540) 955-5160

Pro Tips for Clarke County Tax Sales

Follow these simple tips to make smarter auction decisions:

  • Review listings near conservation areas carefully; local land-use restrictions can affect plans.
  • Older houses might have clear titles, but verify details through the commissioner’s office.
  • Brush up on local regulations—this county enforces property codes consistently
